command:
set -eo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp LC_ALL=C
cd /tmp

echo "== PROJ's own reference vectors, version-matched to the image =="
mkdir -p gie && tar -xf gie.tar -C gie
ls gie | wc -l
# gie exits non-zero on any failure, so capture the output either way -- a dying run must
# leave its evidence, and the assertion below reads this file rather than an exit code.
( cd gie && gie *.gie > /tmp/gie.out 2>&1 ) && GIE_RC=0 || GIE_RC=$?
tail -5 /tmp/gie.out
echo "gie rc=$GIE_RC"

echo "== the raster half: GDAL's warper against a hand-computed block reduction =="
python3 -u - <<'PYEOF' > warp.out 2>&1 || { cat warp.out; exit 1; }
import json, subprocess, time
import numpy as np
import rasterio

with rasterio.open("/tmp/B04.tif") as s:
    arr = s.read(1)
    b, nod, shape = s.bounds, s.nodata, s.shape
res = {"shape": list(shape), "nodata": nod,
       "bounds": [b.left, b.bottom, b.right, b.top]}

# 10 m -> 60 m. 10980 / 6 = 1830 exactly, on the band's own bounds, so every target pixel
# covers exactly 36 source pixels with no partial overlap. Only on an aligned
# integer-factor grid is "GDAL's answer" comparable to "the obvious answer" at all.
F = 6
blocks = arr.reshape(1830, F, 1830, F)
t0 = time.time()
blk_sum = blocks.sum(axis=(1, 3), dtype=np.float64)
# Two different means, and the difference between them is the whole lesson below.
naive_mean = blocks.mean(axis=(1, 3), dtype=np.float64)
nvalid = (blocks > 0).sum(axis=(1, 3))
masked_mean = np.divide(blk_sum, nvalid, out=np.zeros_like(blk_sum), where=nvalid > 0)
res["t_numpy"] = time.time() - t0
res["total"] = float(arr.sum(dtype=np.float64))
res["blocks_with_a_zero"] = int((nvalid < F * F).sum())
res["n_cells"] = int(blk_sum.size)
res["ref_sum_max"] = float(blk_sum.max())
res["ref_mean_max"] = float(masked_mean.max())

def warp(mode, ovr):
    out = f"/tmp/w_{mode}_{ovr}.tif"
    t = time.time()
    subprocess.run(["gdalwarp", "-overwrite", "-q", "-r", mode, "-tr", "60", "60",
                    "-te", str(b.left), str(b.bottom), str(b.right), str(b.top),
                    "-ovr", ovr, "-ot", "Float64", "/tmp/B04.tif", out], check=True)
    el = time.time() - t
    with rasterio.open(out) as d:
        g = d.read(1)
    return g, el

g, el = warp("sum", "NONE")
res["t_sum_NONE"] = el
res["maxdiff_sum_NONE"] = float(np.abs(g - blk_sum).max())
res["ratio_sum_NONE"] = float(g.sum() / blk_sum.sum())

g, el = warp("sum", "AUTO")
res["t_sum_AUTO"] = el
res["ratio_sum_AUTO"] = float(g.sum() / blk_sum.sum())

g, el = warp("average", "NONE")
res["t_average_NONE"] = el
res["maxdiff_average_NONE_naive"] = float(np.abs(g - naive_mean).max())
res["maxdiff_average_NONE_masked"] = float(np.abs(g - masked_mean).max())

# Coordinate round-trip in the geodetic library rather than the raster one: a forward
# transform composed with its inverse is the identity, so this is exact-or-wrong with no
# resampling in the way.
import pyproj
from pyproj import Transformer
res["pyproj"] = pyproj.__version__
res["proj"] = pyproj.proj_version_str
res["rasterio"] = rasterio.__version__
res["gdal"] = rasterio.__gdal_version__
fwd = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:32611", "EPSG:4326", always_xy=True)
inv = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4326", "EPSG:32611", always_xy=True)
corners = [(b.left, b.top), (b.right, b.top), (b.right, b.bottom), (b.left, b.bottom)]
lon, lat = fwd.transform([c[0] for c in corners], [c[1] for c in corners])
x2, y2 = inv.transform(lon, lat)
res["roundtrip_max_m"] = max(max(abs(a - c[0]) for a, c in zip(x2, corners)),
                             max(abs(a - c[1]) for a, c in zip(y2, corners)))
res["corners_lonlat"] = [[round(a, 9), round(c, 9)] for a, c in zip(lon, lat)]
json.dump(res, open("/tmp/warp.json", "w"), indent=1)
print(json.dumps(res, indent=1))
PYEOF
cat warp.out

python3 -u - <<'PYEOF' > smoke-check.txt 2>&1 || { cat smoke-check.txt; exit 1; }
import json, re, sys
fail = []
def check(label, ok, detail):
    print(f"{label:30s} {detail}")
    if not ok: fail.append(label)
def obs(label, detail):
    print(f"{label:30s} {detail}   [observation]")

r = json.load(open("/tmp/warp.json"))
obs("versions", f"rasterio {r['rasterio']} / GDAL {r['gdal']} / "
                f"pyproj {r['pyproj']} on PROJ {r['proj']}")

# ---- PROJ's own committed expected coordinates ------------------------------------
gie = open("/tmp/gie.out").read()
m = re.search(r"Grand total:\s*(\d+)\.\s*Success:\s*(\d+),\s*Skipped:\s*(\d+),\s*"
              r"Failure:\s*(\d+)", gie)
tot, ok, skip, bad = (int(g) for g in m.groups()) if m else (0, 0, 0, -1)
# gie writes this line only after running every file, so its presence is a completion
# sentinel -- a run killed part-way cannot produce it, however many tests had passed.
check("gie_completed", m is not None, "found the Grand total line  want present")
check("gie_test_count", tot == 6191,
      f"{tot} reference vectors  want exactly 6191 (PROJ {r['proj']} test/gie, 12 files)")
check("gie_no_failures", bad == 0 and skip == 0,
      f"{ok} succeeded / {skip} skipped / {bad} FAILED  want 0 failed, 0 skipped")

# ---- GDAL's warper vs a two-line reduction ---------------------------------------
check("aligned_grid", r["shape"] == [10980, 10980] and r["n_cells"] == 1830 * 1830,
      f"{r['shape']} -> {r['n_cells']:,} cells at 6x  want an exact integer factor")
# Independent implementations of the same arithmetic over the same bytes: GDAL's C++
# warper and numpy's reduction. On an aligned grid the answer is DEFINED, so the only
# tolerance is float64 accumulation order -- 3e-07 on values reaching 3.6e+05 is 1e-12
# relative. A cross-code identity, not a band.
check("gdal_sum_eq_numpy", r["maxdiff_sum_NONE"] < 1e-5,
      f"max|gdalwarp -r sum - numpy| = {r['maxdiff_sum_NONE']:.3e} over "
      f"{r['n_cells']:,} cells (values to {r['ref_sum_max']:.0f})  want < 1e-5")
check("sum_conserves_total", abs(r["ratio_sum_NONE"] - 1.0) < 1e-9,
      f"sum(out)/sum(in) = {r['ratio_sum_NONE']:.10f}  want exactly 1 "
      f"(total {r['total']:.0f})")

# Averaging is NOT immune to the band's nodata: GDAL excludes nodata source pixels, so a
# naive numpy mean that counts the zeros answers a different question. Summing IS immune,
# because a zero adds nothing to a sum -- which is why one of these agrees exactly and
# the other does not, and why the fix is the metric rather than either tool.
check("gdal_average_eq_numpy_masked", r["maxdiff_average_NONE_masked"] < 1e-5,
      f"max|gdalwarp -r average - nodata-aware numpy| = "
      f"{r['maxdiff_average_NONE_masked']:.3e}  want < 1e-5")
obs("naive_average_disagrees",
    f"counting the {r['nodata']:.0f}-valued pixels instead gives max|diff| = "
    f"{r['maxdiff_average_NONE_naive']:.3e} on a mean of at most {r['ref_mean_max']:.0f}, "
    f"from just {r['blocks_with_a_zero']} blocks of {r['n_cells']:,} containing a zero")

# The overview trap, reported rather than asserted: pinning the exact factor would make a
# future improvement to GDAL's overview selection fail this check for a GOOD reason, and
# a check that fails for a good reason is still a flaky check.
obs("ovr_auto_reads_a_pyramid",
    f"-ovr AUTO gives sum(out)/sum(in) = {r['ratio_sum_AUTO']:.6f} (~1/16) in "
    f"{r['t_sum_AUTO']:.1f}s, vs {r['t_sum_NONE']:.1f}s for -ovr NONE")

# ---- geodetic round-trip ----------------------------------------------------------
# forward o inverse is the identity, so this is exact to double precision on a 109.8 km
# tile -- 1e-6 m is ~1e-11 relative and has nothing to tune.
check("reproject_roundtrip", r["roundtrip_max_m"] < 1e-6,
      f"32611 -> 4326 -> 32611 recovers the corners to {r['roundtrip_max_m']:.2e} m "
      f"want < 1e-6")
obs("tile_corners_lonlat",
    "; ".join(f"({a:.6f},{c:.6f})" for a, c in r["corners_lonlat"]))
obs("wall_numpy_reduce", f"{r['t_numpy']:.1f}s over 120,560,400 px")
obs("wall_gdalwarp_sum", f"{r['t_sum_NONE']:.1f}s (-ovr NONE, full resolution)")

if fail:
    print("FAILED: " + ", ".join(fail)); sys.exit(1)
PYEOF
cat smoke-check.txt
echo "SMOKE CHECK PASSED"
